title: posthog-cli crate: API bundle is gitignored, so include list and --allow-dirty must stay in sync
answers: Why does cargo publish for posthog-cli need --allow-dirty?
posthog-cli api is dead in the crates.io crate
Adding a new file the posthog-cli build needs to cli/Cargo.toml include
body:
cli/lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs is gitignored and written during the release, so cargo would not package it by default.
- cli/Cargo.toml `include` lists it explicitly: src/**/*, build.rs, lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs, README.md.
- An explicit `include` REPLACES cargo's tracked-files default. Any new path the build needs (new build input, embedded asset) must be added there or consumers' `cargo install` builds break.
- The publish-cargo job in .github/workflows/release-cli.yml runs `cargo publish -p posthog-cli --allow-dirty` because the bundle is always untracked in the checkout.
- Verify with `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` in cli/.
applies: cli/Cargo.toml packaging and the publish-cargo job in release-cli.yml
says: Publishing our command-line tool fails with dirty files

search: The posthog-cli crate must explicitly include its gitignored API bundle (lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs, written during release) in cli/Cargo.toml's `include` list alongside src/**/* and build.rs, because explicit include replaces cargo's default tracked-files behavior. Any new build input or embedded asset must be added to the include list or `cargo install` will break for consumers. The release workflow (.github/workflows/release-cli.yml) uses `cargo publish -p posthog-cli --allow-dirty` because the bundle stays untracked; verify changes with `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` in cli/.
